description: Prober eval cases. Each case is one person's material for one domain, shaped exactly like the prober input. `planted` lists contradictions the prober must find (at least one probe must reference one of the listed ids); `expect_zero` cases contain no contradiction and must produce zero probes. Only the seven templates are allowed (enforced by the output schema).

planted.description: high self-rated authoritative (reasoning, warmth) with scenario answers that are entirely about control and obedience

answers.question_text: On a normal day, how do you show a child warmth? A concrete example from this week if there was one.
answers.answer_text: I make sure she does what she is told. Yesterday she left her shoes out and I had her redo it three times until it was right.

answers.question_text: On a normal day, how do you enforce a limit? A concrete example.
answers.answer_text: No discussion. She lost her tablet for the week on Tuesday for talking back and that is that.

answers.question_text: Finish this sentence: A respectful child is one who ____.
answers.answer_text: does what an adult says the first time, without questions.

answers.question_text: Describe a moment where a child was corrected well. What made it good?
answers.answer_text: Last week my son interrupted and I sent him to his room until dinner. It was good because he did not do it again.

tags.comment: Children do not question adults. It looks like a quiet house.

planted.description: respect defined as obedience and not talking back, alongside adult conduct (shouting, swearing) the person would not accept from the child

answers.question_text: Finish this sentence: A respectful child is one who ____.
answers.answer_text: never raises their voice to an adult and never swears at anyone.

answers.question_text: Name something adults in the house do that you would not want the child to copy.
answers.answer_text: Honestly nothing comes to mind. We are pretty careful.

answers.question_text: Is it fine for adults to use language or habits around a child that the child isn't allowed to use? Where's the line?
answers.answer_text: Yes, adults are adults. I swear when I am angry and I yell at my partner when the kids are in the next room. They know the difference.

answers.question_text: Describe what good would look like here, concretely, in your house, on an ordinary week.
answers.answer_text: On a normal Tuesday the kids come in from school, say hello, do homework at the table without arguing, and speak to us politely at dinner.

tags.comment: Kids hold a standard of language. Met when nobody swears at the table.

planted.description: an easygoing, low-structure self-description (high permissive) while asking for an ideal weekday that is fully scheduled; or a self-description of being easygoing with no structure the person can name when asked

answers.question_text: How much of a child's day should be planned versus open? Describe your ideal weekday.
answers.answer_text: Up at 6:45, breakfast at 7, school, piano at 4, homework 5 to 6, dinner at 6:30, reading 7 to 7:30, lights out at 8. Weekends the same with sport instead of school.

answers.question_text: On a normal day, how do you enforce a limit? A concrete example.
answers.answer_text: I am really relaxed about it. I let things unfold and we do not really have rules as such. I cannot think of a limit I enforced this week.

answers.question_text: Describe the balance of structure and freedom you'd want for a child at this age.
answers.answer_text: Mostly freedom. Kids should be kids. Last Saturday she chose everything we did and that was fine.

other_answers.question_text: One of you wants to reorganize a shared space the other uses. What's the right way to go about it?
other_answers.answer_text: Ask first, then do it together on a Sunday like we did with the pantry last month.

tags.comment: A light routine. Met when bedtime is roughly the same each night.

planted.description: tags the split a requirement, then describes being content with any split as long as it is discussed

answers.question_text: One of you wants to reorganize a shared space the other uses. What's the right way to go about it?
answers.answer_text: Say it out loud first. When I moved the mugs last month without saying, it was a whole thing at breakfast.

answers.question_text: On the tasks that flagged, describe the split you'd actually be content with.
answers.answer_text: Honestly any split is fine with me as long as we talk about it. Sixty-forty, fifty-fifty, whatever. Last week he did all the cooking and I did not mind at all.

tags.comment: The cooking and dishes split must be exactly even. Met when we each cook three nights and split the seventh.

answers.question_text: Your partner's face looks angry and you don't know if they are. What do you do? What should they do?
answers.answer_text: I ask. Last Thursday I said 'you look tense, is it me?' and she said it was work. She should say so before I ask, but asking is fine.

answers.question_text: Your partner has been quiet for two days. What do you assume, and what do you do?
answers.answer_text: I assume work or family. After a day I ask directly, like in March when her mother was ill and she went quiet.

answers.question_text: When you're upset, how do you want to be approached, in words you'd actually use?
answers.answer_text: 'I can see something is up. Want to talk now or later?' Then give me the later if I take it.

tags.comment: Being asked rather than read. Met when she checks before assuming.

answers.question_text: One of you initiates a kiss with no other intention and the other isn't in the mood. Write the exchange.
answers.answer_text: Me: quick kiss on the way past. Him: 'not now, long day.' Me: 'okay, tea?' That happened Sunday and it was fine.

answers.question_text: What's the smallest thing your partner could do that would make you feel wanted this week?
answers.answer_text: Text me at lunch on Wednesday for no reason, like he did two weeks ago.

answers.question_text: Describe an ordinary good week, with affection in it, under current circumstances. Then a year from now.
answers.answer_text: Now: a kiss most mornings, one evening on the sofa together, one date every other week. In a year, with the baby sleeping: the same plus one night away a quarter.

tags.comment: Advance notice for plans. Met when date night is on the calendar by Monday.

answers.question_text: One of you says something hurtful in a fight. Ten minutes later, what happens? The next morning?
What does a pause in a fight mean to you, and what would make you trust that it isn't abandonment?
answers.answer_text: A pause means twenty minutes apart and a time to come back. When she said 'back at nine' last month and came back at nine, I trusted it.

answers.question_text: Describe a fight that went as well as a fight can.
answers.answer_text: The car argument in June: we both got loud, she called a pause, we came back after dinner and each said what we got wrong.

tags.comment: An apology within the day. Met when neither of us goes to bed on it.
